"STORYVERSE AI — THE FUTURE OF STORYTELLING

Create a premium, futuristic AI entertainment application called STORYVERSE AI.

MAIN PURPOSE:

Build an application that allows users to photograph books, comics, documents, handwritten stories, recipes, newspapers, and other text-based materials and transform them into immersive cinematic audio storytelling experiences.

MAIN SCREEN:

- Beautiful black and deep-purple cinematic interface.
- Large glowing SCAN ANYTHING button.
- Camera upload and photo gallery options.
- Recently created experiences.
- Featured stories and genres.
- Premium, professional entertainment-app design.

CORE FEATURES:

1. AI SCANNER: Use the camera to photograph text and extract readable content using OCR.

2. CINEMATIC NARRATOR: Convert extracted text into natural, expressive narration.

3. MULTIPLE CHARACTERS: Identify dialogue and assign different realistic voices to individual characters.

4. CINEMATIC AUDIO: Generate appropriate background music, environmental sounds, dramatic effects, suspense, and emotional atmosphere.

5. GENRE SELECTOR: Horror, thriller, fantasy, science fiction, romance, comedy, mystery, and adventure.

6. VISUAL EXPERIENCE: Generate cinematic scene illustrations and optional animated scenes to accompany narration.

7. STORY LIBRARY: Save, organize, replay, and continue previous experiences.

8. VOICE CUSTOMIZATION: Allow users to select narration styles, character voices, accents, and playback speeds.

9. LANGUAGE SUPPORT: Support multiple languages and translation where available.

10. ORIGINAL STORY CREATOR: Allow users to write their own stories and transform them into cinematic productions.

IMPORTANT:

The application must have a functional interface, working navigation, camera/upload workflow, and realistic demonstrations of its features. Connect actual AI, OCR, text-to-speech, and audio-generation services where supported. Do not present simulated features as fully functional.

Respect copyright: support public-domain works, licensed content, original writing, and content users are authorized to process.

BUSINESS MODEL:

- Free introductory tier.
- Premium monthly subscription.
- Unlimited or expanded cinematic experiences on higher tiers.
- Premium character voices.
- Premium visual storytelling.
- Creator tools.

DESIGN GOAL:

Make STORYVERSE AI look and feel like a billion-dollar entertainment technology company. It should look polished, futuristic, cinematic, addictive to explore, and simple enough for anyone to use.

TAGLINE: DON'T JUST READ IT. EXPERIENCE IT.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.

## Objective
- Build a polished STORYVERSE AI storytelling application from the user’s brief, with functional navigation, camera/upload and OCR workflow, story creation/library, and playable narration.

## Requirements
- Cinematic black/deep-purple design; responsive interface; tagline “DON'T JUST READ IT. EXPERIENCE IT.”
- Support authorized content, public-domain works, and original writing; do not portray simulated AI capabilities as real.
- Include camera/photo upload, OCR, narration, genres, story library, creator options, and business-model presentation.
- Verify with a small JPEG screenshot and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript app without a backend.
- Be explicit that narration and soundscape use browser-native/local capabilities; AI narration, character voices, generation, cloud storage, and billing are not connected.
- OCR uses Tesseract.js loaded from jsDelivr on demand; plain-text uploads work locally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built premium responsive home, library, story detail, and story creator screens with sample stories and genre navigation.
- Implemented localStorage story persistence, text-file import, image upload with browser OCR, camera capture, browser speech synthesis, synthesized ambient tones, and clear feature limitations.
- `node --check app.js` passed.
- Started local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/storyverse.jpg`.

### Active
- Browser interaction verification; a navigation click was just attempted, but no follow-up result has been checked.

### Blocked
- Browser verification initially blocked because Chromium was not installed; `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` subsequently completed, so this is resolved.
- Browser reported a favicon 404 (`http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico`); no favicon has been added.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser QA: verify creator navigation, create/save/play flow, library filtering, and upload/camera/OCR UI.
2. Fix any issues found and optionally add a favicon to clear the console 404.
3. Report remaining limitations honestly, especially no connected AI generation, character voice assignment, or subscription/billing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App structure and page layouts.
- `styles.css`: Responsive cinematic styling.
- `app.js`: Navigation, local stories, OCR, camera, narration, soundscape, and interactions.
- `screenshots/storyverse.jpg`: Latest captured homepage screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Application is served at `http://localhost:3002`.
- `playwright-cli` session is open; latest screenshot was taken before further browser interaction.
- `app.js` includes demo content and explicitly labels limitations; it does not connect to external AI/TTS generation services.

  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:

  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs

Storage:

  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions

  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify a polished STORYVERSE AI storytelling app with navigation, story creation and library, image/text import, OCR, and narration.

## Requirements
- Cinematic black/deep-purple design, responsive layout, and tagline “DON'T JUST READ IT. EXPERIENCE IT.”
- Support authorized content, public-domain works, and original writing; clearly disclose simulated or unavailable AI features.
- Include camera/photo upload, OCR, narration, genres, story library, creator options, and business-model presentation.
- Verify with a small JPEG screenshot and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript app without a backend.
- Narration and soundscape use browser-native/local capabilities; AI narration, generation, character voices, cloud storage, and billing are not connected.
- OCR uses Tesseract.js from jsDelivr on demand; text-file imports work locally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive home, library, story detail, and story creator screens with sample stories and genre navigation.
- Implemented localStorage story persistence, text import, image upload with browser OCR UI, camera capture UI, browser speech synthesis, synthesized ambient tones, and feature-limit disclosures.
- `node --check app.js` passed.
- Browser-tested navigation, story creation/save, library search, and text-file import.
- Added an inline SVG favicon to `index.html`.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/storyverse.jpg`.

### Active
- Continue browser QA: verify OCR extraction, confirm favicon change clears the console 404, and investigate narration startup failure.
- Clean up the QA-created “QA Sample Story” from browser localStorage if it should not remain in the demo data.

### Blocked
- Browser narration attempt failed with “Narration could not start. Try another browser voice.”
- Camera testing is blocked by the browser environment reporting “Requested device not found”; the UI provides an upload alternative.

## Next Move
1. Reload the app and check whether the favicon 404 is resolved.
2. Investigate browser speech synthesis failure and retest narration where a device voice is available.
3. Run OCR extraction on an image and check its result; camera capture cannot be verified without a camera device.
4. Remove QA test data from localStorage if appropriate, then rerun relevant checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App structure and inline SVG favicon.
- `styles.css`: Responsive cinematic styling.
- `app.js`: Navigation, story persistence, OCR, camera, narration, soundscape, and interactions.
- `screenshots/storyverse.jpg`: Captured homepage screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- App is served at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Browser QA created “QA Sample Story” and browser localStorage now contains four stories; a text import test also populated the creator form.
- Browser console previously showed a favicon 404; the favicon link was added afterward but has not yet been verified after reload.
- No connected AI generation, character voice assignment, subscription, or billing.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify a polished STORYVERSE storytelling app.
- New request: “Make it so you take a picture of the book and it reads it to you like a film.”

## Requirements
- Cinematic black/deep-purple design, responsive layout, tagline “DON'T JUST READ IT. EXPERIENCE IT.”
- Support authorized content, public-domain works, and original writing; disclose simulated or unavailable AI features.
- Provide camera/photo upload, OCR, narration, genres, story library, creator options, and business-model presentation.
- Verify with a small JPEG screenshot and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript app without a backend.
- OCR uses Tesseract.js via jsDelivr; speech narration uses browser-native voices; soundscape uses synthesized browser audio.
- AI narration/generation, cinematic video production, character voices, cloud storage, and billing are not connected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built home, library, story detail, and story creator screens with sample stories and genre navigation.
- Added local story persistence, text import, image upload/OCR, camera capture UI, browser speech synthesis, synthesized ambient tones, and feature disclosures.
- `node --check app.js` passes.
- Browser QA verified navigation, story creation/save, library search, text import, OCR extraction, and inline SVG favicon.
- Improved narration error handling in `app.js`; isolated Chromium had no speech voices and returned narration errors.
- Existing screenshot: `screenshots/storyverse.jpg`, 1050 × 793 JPEG.

### Active
- Implement the latest request: photograph a book page, extract text, then present it as a more film-like narrated experience. No changes for this new request have been made yet.

### Blocked
- Camera capture cannot be verified in the current browser environment: no camera device found.
- Narration cannot be verified in the isolated Chromium environment: no voices available; errors included `not-allowed` and `synthesis-failed`.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and update `app.js` so a captured/uploaded page can move smoothly from OCR into an immersive narration experience without manually recreating a story.
2. Enhance the listening experience with film-like visual presentation using available browser capabilities, while clearly disclosing limits and avoiding claims of connected AI/video generation.
3. Test OCR-to-play flow and responsive visuals; retest narration where a device speech voice is available.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App UI and inline SVG favicon.
- `styles.css`: Responsive cinematic styling and player styles.
- `app.js`: OCR, camera, narration, story creation, and navigation logic.
- `screenshots/storyverse.jpg`: Existing homepage screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- App is served at `http://localhost:3002`.
- QA used isolated Chromium profiles; the prior browser profile still has a QA-created “QA Sample Story” and text import state in localStorage.

## Objective
- Build and verify STORYVERSE, a cinematic storytelling app for authorized text, public-domain works, and original writing.
- Use an in-browser pretrained AI voice model for narration instead of browser speech synthesis.

## Requirements
- Cinematic black/deep-purple design, responsive layout, and tagline “DON'T JUST READ IT. EXPERIENCE IT.”
- Support photo capture/upload, OCR, narration, genres, story library, creator options, and business-model presentation.
- Accurately disclose available, simulated, and unavailable features; do not claim the app trains its own model.

## Decisions
- Use a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript app without a backend.
- Use Kokoro TTS with `kokoro-js`, model `onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX`, `dtype: "q8"`, and `device: "wasm"`.
- Download the pretrained model on first use; run speech generation locally in the browser.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the app screens, story library and creator, local persistence, OCR review, and cinematic photo-backed player.
- Replaced `SpeechSynthesisUtterance` playback with Kokoro model loading, chunked audio generation/playback, pause/resume, progress, and failure messaging.
- Updated narration disclosures and documentation to describe the pretrained model, first-use download, and local inference.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed; no stale browser speech-synthesis references were found.
- Captured a home-page screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/storyverse-home.jpg`.

### Active
- Verify Kokoro playback, model-load failure handling, OCR-to-cinematic flow, and responsive visuals in a browser.

### Blocked
- Camera capture was not verifiable in the earlier browser environment because no camera device was found.
- Kokoro runtime playback has not yet been verified.

## Next Move
1. Test narration playback and error handling in a browser with network access; verify the `kokoro-js` API integration.
2. Test OCR-to-cinematic playback and responsive visuals; update `screenshots/storyverse.jpg` if appropriate.
3. Re-run syntax and diff checks after any fixes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Kokoro integration, OCR, story flow, and cinematic player.
- `index.html`: App screens and disclosures.
- `styles.css`: Cinematic player and responsive styling.
- `README.md`: Narration implementation and privacy/download notes.
- `screenshots/storyverse.jpg`: Existing repository screenshot.

## Important Context
- Kokoro library is dynamically imported from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/kokoro-js@1.2.1/+esm`.
- Repository changes are uncommitted; `app.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and other project files appear untracked, while `README.md` is modified.
- A screenshot command succeeded against `http://localhost:3002`; a separate attempt to start a local server failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`.

## Objective
- Build and verify STORYVERSE, a cinematic storytelling app for authorized text, public-domain works, and original writing.
- Use an in-browser pretrained AI voice model for narration rather than browser speech synthesis.

## Requirements
- Cinematic black/deep-purple design, responsive layout, and tagline “DON'T JUST READ IT. EXPERIENCE IT.”
- Support photo capture/upload, OCR, narration, genres, story library, creator options, and business-model presentation.
- Accurately disclose available, simulated, and unavailable features; do not claim the app trains its own model.

## Decisions
- Use a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript app without a backend.
- Use Kokoro TTS with `kokoro-js`, model `onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX`, `dtype: "q8"`, and `device: "wasm"`.
- Download the pretrained model on first use; run speech generation locally in the browser.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the app screens, story library and creator, local persistence, OCR review, and cinematic photo-backed player.
- Integrated Kokoro narration with chunked audio generation/playback, pause/resume, progress, and failure messaging.
- Verified Kokoro model loading and audible-playback state in Chromium; status reached “The story is unfolding,” caption displayed, and no overflow at 780×437.
- Verified OCR on a generated sample image, reviewed extracted text, and created a scanned story that opened in the cinematic player.
- Checked home, library, create, detail, and cinema layouts at 1440, 768, and 390px widths; no horizontal overflow there.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed; no stale browser speech-synthesis references were found.
- Saved a fresh 1440×900 home screenshot to `/tmp/opencode/storyverse-final.jpg`.

### Active
- Fix and recheck horizontal overflow on the home page at 320px; measured `scrollWidth: 345` at a 320px viewport.
- Test narration model-load failure handling; refresh `screenshots/storyverse.jpg` if appropriate.

### Blocked
- Camera capture cannot be verified because Chromium reported `Requested device not found`.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and fix the 320px home-page overflow in `styles.css`, then rerun the responsive checks.
2. Exercise Kokoro model-load failure handling and verify user-facing messaging.
3. Refresh `screenshots/storyverse.jpg` if the new screenshot is suitable; rerun syntax and diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Kokoro integration, OCR, story flow, and cinematic player.
- `index.html`: App screens and disclosures.
- `styles.css`: Cinematic player, responsive layout, and the 320px overflow area.
- `README.md`: Narration implementation and privacy/download notes.
- `screenshots/storyverse.jpg`: Existing repository screenshot to consider refreshing.

## Important Context
- Kokoro library is dynamically imported from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/kokoro-js@1.2.1/+esm`.
- App is reachable at `http://localhost:3002`; Chromium remote debugging is on port `9222`.
- Changes remain uncommitted: `README.md` is modified; `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `app.js`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `styles.css` are untracked.
- The repo screenshot has not been refreshed; the new screenshot is only at `/tmp/opencode/storyverse-final.jpg`.

## Objective
- Build and verify STORYVERSE, a cinematic storytelling app for authorized text, public-domain works, and original writing.
- Use an in-browser pretrained AI voice model for narration rather than browser speech synthesis.

## Requirements
- Cinematic black/deep-purple design, responsive layout, and tagline “DON'T JUST READ IT. EXPERIENCE IT.”
- Support photo capture/upload, OCR, narration, genres, story library, creator options, and business-model presentation.
- Accurately disclose available, simulated, and unavailable features; do not claim the app trains its own model.

## Decisions
- Use a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript app without a backend.
- Use Kokoro TTS with `kokoro-js`, model `onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX`, `dtype: "q8"`, and `device: "wasm"`.
- Download the pretrained model on first use; run speech generation locally in the browser.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built app screens, story library and creator, local persistence, OCR review, and cinematic photo-backed player.
- Integrated Kokoro narration with chunked audio generation/playback, pause/resume, progress, and failure messaging.
- Verified Kokoro model loading and audible-playback state in Chromium; status reached “The story is unfolding,” caption displayed, and no overflow at 780×437.
- Verified OCR on a generated sample image, reviewed extracted text, and created a scanned story that opened in the cinematic player.
- Checked home, library, create, detail, and cinema layouts at 1440, 768, and 390px widths; no horizontal overflow there.
- Fixed the 320px home overflow by constraining `.quick-actions` grid tracks and `.quick-card`, and adjusting `.scan-button`; subsequent check reported no document horizontal overflow at 320px.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed previously; no stale browser speech-synthesis references were found.
- Saved a fresh 1440×900 home screenshot to `/tmp/opencode/storyverse-final.jpg`.

### Active
- Test Kokoro model-load failure handling and verify user-facing messaging.
- Refresh `screenshots/storyverse.jpg` if the fresh screenshot is suitable; rerun syntax and diff checks after CSS changes.

### Blocked
- Camera capture cannot be verified because Chromium reported `Requested device not found`.

## Next Move
1. Exercise Kokoro model-load failure handling and confirm the status message.
2. Review `/tmp/opencode/storyverse-final.jpg`; refresh `screenshots/storyverse.jpg` if appropriate.
3. Rerun responsive checks, `node --check app.js`, and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Kokoro integration, OCR, story flow, and cinematic player.
- `index.html`: App screens and disclosures.
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout and recent 320px overflow adjustments.
- `README.md`: Narration implementation and privacy/download notes.
- `screenshots/storyverse.jpg`: Existing repository screenshot to consider refreshing.
- `/tmp/opencode/storyverse-final.jpg`: Fresh screenshot candidate.

## Important Context
- Kokoro library is dynamically imported from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/kokoro-js@1.2.1/+esm`.
- App is reachable at `http://localhost:3002`; Chromium remote debugging is on port `9222`.
- Changes are uncommitted: `README.md` modified; `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `app.js`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `styles.css` untracked.
